title: An SCS/Kubernetes-hosted Switchboard proves sovereignty at the record layer, not just the VM layer
content:
This group proposes a deployment rather than an integration: Switchboard running on the partner's own SCS/Kubernetes platform as a reference deployment in their stack. The claim attached to it is a distinction — sovereignty proven at the record layer, not just the VM layer.

That distinction is the substance. Sovereign cloud arguments usually stop at where the machines run and who can be compelled to hand them over. They say nothing about whether the business record itself — the attributed history of what was decided — is held in a form the operator controls, or whether it lives inside a vendor application that merely happens to run on sovereign infrastructure. Moving the record layer onto the same sovereign platform closes the gap the infrastructure argument leaves open.

The single lead is GONICUS GmbH, recorded as 80-plus staff in Arnsberg with Bonn and Duesseldorf presence, marked "2 · next". For a partner whose pitch is already sovereignty, this extends an argument they make rather than introducing one they do not.
